title: Response overlay renders prebuilt markdown HTML without a local sanitization boundary
reasoning: Default response entries are injected with dangerouslySetInnerHTML using entry.markdownHtml. The excerpt does not show a local DOMPurify/sanitization step or an invariant check before injection, even though this renderer has DOMPurify available. If markdownHtml is derived from assistant/tool/search content, a malicious model output or tool result could execute HTML/script-like payloads in the Electron renderer context. This is higher impact than ordinary web XSS because the renderer participates in desktop app IPC and local workflows.
recommendation: Sanitize markdownHtml at the rendering boundary, or change the response overlay contract so it only accepts a branded/sanitized HTML value created by a single sanitizer module. Add tests that prove scriptable HTML, event handlers, javascript: URLs, and unsafe SVG/MathML payloads are removed before rendering.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were included for ChatBoxResponse or the response overlay HTML contract, and the component currently accepts markdownHtml directly.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a renderer/unit test for ChatBoxResponse or the overlay view model that renders a response entry containing unsafe HTML and asserts no unsafe attributes/elements survive in the DOM.
minimumFixScope: ChatBoxResponse rendering boundary plus the response-overlay markdown/sanitizer contract used to create entry.markdownHtml.
